en.name: Our Lady of Banneux
en.summary: 1933 apparitions to an eleven-year-old girl in Belgium, in which the Virgin identified herself as the "Virgin of the Poor."
en.body: In January 1933, shortly after the apparitions at nearby Beauraing had concluded, an eleven-year-old girl named Mariette Beco in the Belgian village of Banneux reported the Virgin Mary appearing to her in her family's garden and leading her, over a series of eight apparitions, to a small spring nearby. Mary reportedly identified herself to Mariette as the "Virgin of the Poor" and asked that a chapel be built at the spring, saying the water was intended for the relief of the sick of all nations, and that she had come to relieve suffering. Mariette's family was not notably religious, which investigators later regarded as lending credibility to accounts that were otherwise difficult to dismiss as coached or expected behavior. The apparitions were formally approved by the local bishop in 1949, and the spring at Banneux continues to draw pilgrims seeking healing.
